note: This is a directional self-assessment, not legal advice. Requirements vary by jurisdiction, interpretation, and your specific data flows. Engage qualified counsel before making compliance commitments.

data_types.name: Personal identifiers (names, emails, IPs, device IDs)
Sensitive PII (SSN, government ID, financial account, precise location)

deployment_models.name: SaaS multi-tenant (vendor hosts data)
deployment_models.notes: Vendor subprocessors, shared infra, and customer data segregation add compliance surface area.

deployment_models.name: SaaS single-tenant / VPC
deployment_models.notes: Isolated tenancy reduces some breach blast radius.

deployment_models.name: Self-hosted / on-prem
deployment_models.notes: You own patching, access controls, logs, and physical/logical security.

deployment_models.name: Hybrid (some data in cloud, some local)
deployment_models.notes: Data residency and cross-border transfer rules become more complex.

deployment_models.name: Edge / on-device
deployment_models.notes: Local processing can reduce server-side data exposure, but device security and telemetry still matter.

features.name: Trains or fine-tunes on user data

frameworks.name: GDPR
frameworks.summary: Lawful basis, purpose limitation, data minimization, rights requests, DPA, SCCs, DPIA for high-risk processing.

frameworks.name: UK DPA 2018
frameworks.summary: UK-specific GDPR implementation; separate representative and ICO registration may apply.

frameworks.name: EU AI Act
frameworks.summary: Risk classification, CE marking for high-risk AI, transparency, human oversight, fundamental-rights impact assessment.

frameworks.name: CCPA/CPRA
frameworks.full_name: California Consumer Privacy Act / Rights Act
frameworks.summary: Privacy policy, consumer rights (know, delete, opt-out, correct), service-provider contracts, data minimization.

frameworks.name: US State Privacy Laws
frameworks.full_name: VA, CO, CT, UT, TX and similar state laws
frameworks.summary: Add-on rights and opt-out requirements beyond CCPA; often similar but not identical.

frameworks.name: PIPEDA
frameworks.summary: Consent, purpose limitation, safeguards, breach notification, access/correction rights.

frameworks.name: LGPD
frameworks.full_name: Brazil Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados
frameworks.summary: Legal bases, rights of data subjects, DPO requirement for certain controllers, ANPD reporting.

frameworks.name: Singapore PDPA
frameworks.summary: Consent, purpose limitation, DPO, data-breach notification, accountability and data-protection-by-design.

frameworks.name: Japan APPI
frameworks.full_name: Act on Protection of Personal Information
frameworks.summary: Opt-in consent for third-party transfers, rights to disclosure/correction/cessation, cross-border transfer rules.

frameworks.name: South Korea PIPA
frameworks.summary: Consent, data minimization, pseudonymization, PI processing policy, breach notification to PIPC.

frameworks.name: India DPDPA
frameworks.summary: Consent-based framework, DPO and grievance officer for Significant Data Fiduciaries, data-principal rights.

frameworks.name: UAE PDPL
frameworks.summary: Consent, lawful bases, cross-border transfer rules, data subject rights, DPO for high-risk processing.

frameworks.name: Saudi PDPL
frameworks.summary: Consent, localization preferences for sensitive data, DPO, rights requests, breach notification to SDAIA.

frameworks.name: HIPAA
frameworks.full_name: US Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
frameworks.summary: BAA, PHI safeguards, minimum necessary, access controls, audit logs, breach notification, risk analysis.

frameworks.name: FERPA
frameworks.full_name: US Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act
frameworks.summary: School official exceptions, consent for disclosures, education-record safeguards, directory-information policies.

frameworks.name: GLBA
frameworks.summary: Privacy notice, opt-out, safeguards rule, financial data security program, incident response plan.

frameworks.name: PCI DSS
frameworks.full_name: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
frameworks.summary: Required if cardholder data is stored, processed, or transmitted. Network segmentation, encryption, access controls, scans.

frameworks.name: COPPA
frameworks.full_name: US Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule
frameworks.summary: Verifiable parental consent, data minimization, privacy policy, retention limits for under-13 users.

frameworks.name: FTC Act / AI guidance
frameworks.full_name: US FTC Section 5 and AI enforcement
frameworks.summary: Prohibition on unfair or deceptive practices; truthful claims, algorithmic fairness, and consumer harm prevention.

frameworks.name: DSA / Digital Services Act
frameworks.summary: Transparency reporting, illegal content processes, traceability, terms-and-conditions obligations for intermediary platforms.

frameworks.name: Canada Voluntary AI Code
frameworks.full_name: Canadian Voluntary Code of Conduct on AI
frameworks.summary: Voluntary commitments on transparency, fairness, human oversight, and accountability.

frameworks.name: Australia Privacy Act
frameworks.summary: APPs, privacy policy, collection notice, access/correction, data breach notification, cross-border accountability.

frameworks.name: OAIC AI guidance
frameworks.summary: Privacy-by-design, transparency, fairness, accuracy, and rights-respecting AI guidance.

frameworks.name: Singapore IMDA GenAI
frameworks.summary: Voluntary model AI governance: accountability, data, trusted development and deployment, incident reporting.

frameworks.name: India AI Ethics / Advisory
frameworks.full_name: India AI advisory and ethics principles
frameworks.summary: Voluntary advisory on non-personal data, user consent, labeling AI-generated content, and deepfake mitigation.

frameworks.name: FedRAMP
frameworks.full_name: US Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program
frameworks.summary: Required for US federal cloud services. Extensive NIST 800-53 controls, continuous monitoring, 3PAO assessment.

frameworks.name: Equal Employment / AI hiring rules
frameworks.full_name: EEOC, NYC Local Law 144, EU equal treatment
frameworks.summary: Bias audits, notice, consent, and disparate-impact review for AI used in employment decisions.

frameworks.name: SOC 2 Type II
frameworks.summary: Security, availability, confidentiality, and privacy trust services. Widely expected by enterprise buyers.

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 27701
frameworks.summary: Privacy-focused extension to ISO 27001; useful for international privacy program alignment.

controls.text: Publish a clear privacy policy covering data collection, purposes, retention, rights, and contact details.
Execute Data Processing / Service-Provider Agreements with every subprocessor and cloud provider.
Collect and retain only the personal data strictly needed for the stated purpose.
Document and enforce data-retention and deletion schedules.
Support account/data deletion requests and propagate deletion to backups and subprocessors.
Encrypt data in transit using TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites.
Encrypt stored personal data and model artifacts at rest.
Role-based access controls, MFA, and least-privilege for production data and models.
Log access, changes, and data exports; retain logs per policy and review periodically.
Document the lawful basis for processing and support opt-in/withdrawal where required.
Implement a process for access, correction, deletion, portability, and opt-out requests.
Maintain an incident-response and breach-notification playbook with defined timelines.
Conduct a Data Protection / Privacy Impact Assessment for high-risk processing.
Use SCCs, adequacy decisions, BCRs, or other lawful cross-border transfer mechanisms.
Offer region-specific hosting or processing to meet localization requirements.
Maintain and publish a subprocessor / third-party model-provider inventory.
Train staff and contractors on privacy obligations, phishing, and incident escalation.
Obtain explicit opt-in consent before using personal data to train or fine-tune models.
Provide an opt-out or data-sale opt-out mechanism where required.
Review whether training data is truly anonymized or pseudonymized and document residual re-identification risk.
Design meaningful human oversight for high-risk or automated decision outputs.
Provide plain-language explanations of how the agent reaches significant outputs or decisions.
Assess and document bias / fairness risks for decisions affecting people.
Filter or sanitize user inputs to reject PII overload, injection, and abuse.
Filter outputs to reduce leakage of training data, PII, or harmful content.
Apply rate limits, abuse detection, and usage quotas to public endpoints.
Monitor for jailbreaks, prompt injection, data exfiltration attempts, and misuse.
Monitor and alert on unexpected data egress from agent tools and APIs.
Disclose AI-generated content and label outputs as machine-generated where required.
For EU high-risk AI systems, prepare technical documentation and conformity assessment.
Publish periodic transparency reports on content moderation, risks, and complaints.
Sign Business Associate Agreements for any HIPAA-covered PHI processing.
Apply minimum-necessary access to PHI and document disclosures.
Confirm education-record processing meets school-official or consent requirements.
Obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting children's personal data.
Scope and segment cardholder data environment; never store full track or CVV data.
Maintain a written information-security program for financial customer data.
Appoint a Data Protection Officer or privacy lead where required.
Review LLM / vector DB / cloud provider security, privacy, and AI policies annually.
Maintain an inventory of models, data sources, training datasets, and release versions.
